newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares surge 2.2 pct, Hindustan Lever strong.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares surge 2.2 pct, Hindustan Lever strong.

text.p: Delhi shares closed sharply higher on Tuesday on strong purchases by foreign investors and speculators fuelled by news of Hindustan Lever Ltd's first-half results, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 20.42 points, or 2.18 percent, higher at 957.55.
Hindustan Lever on Tuesday set an interim dividend of 7.5 rupees for calander 1997.
It said net profit in the first six months to June 30 totalled 2.56 billion rupees, which included that of its merged affiliate Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd.
The share jumped 20.60 rupees to close at 1,545.50.
"With the extension of the bull phase, retail investors also turned active and made increased purchases in some of the lesser traded shares," said S.C. Garg of brokers Jindal Securities.
Another broker said: "Easy liquidity in the market also helped spur buying."
ITC shot up 35.50 rupees to 580.50 on institutional buying, brokers said.
State Bank of India firmed 9.55 rupees to 339.25.
Bajaj Auto ended six rupees higher at 926.
